column1: # DOCUMENT TOKEN BRIDGE -- what doc-render-engine calls a token, and which
# canonical role it actually is.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS DATA
# doc-render-engine/theme/colors.tsv is a nine-token stand-in written in an
# afternoon to unblock a demo. Its own header says so and puts itself on death
# row. But it did NOT invent nine new colours -- it invented nine new NAMES for
# colours this design system already owns, and then a tenth that is genuinely
# new. Until someone writes that down, the refit looks like a merge of two
# palettes. It is a rename of nine and an addition of one.
# Data, not prose, and not code, for the reason contrast-budget.tsv is data: a
# mapping in a paragraph cannot be diffed, cannot be consumed, and cannot be
# checked. A row can.
# THIS FILE IS A WAYPOINT, NOT A HOME. The registry already owns this exact
# mechanism -- registry/_index.json fmpRoleMap maps the retired FileMaker cv-*
# layout roles onto the same contract, and resolve.js consumes it as aliasMap.
# A renderer map is a SECOND INSTANCE of one mechanism, not a second mechanism,
# so it belongs beside that one. It is not there yet on purpose: tokenKeys in
# that file is hand-typed and stale by five entries (D2), and the ruled fix is
# to DERIVE it from the vectors/colors.tsv header row rather than hand-patch
# it. One pass touches the registry, structurally, not two. Fold this in during
# THAT pass and retire this file to a stub. If a THIRD consumer map appears
# before then, stop and promote all of them to a single roleMaps object --
# three siblings is the sprawl this repo exists to refuse.
# COLUMNS
# consumer    the renderer's token name, as it appears in its colors.tsv
# canonical   the role in registry/_index.json tokenRoles
# status      alias  = a pure rename, no design change, safe today
#             new    = no canonical equivalent, a design-system decision
# note        why, and anything the refit must not get wrong
consumer
surface
surface-raised
column4: Cards, admonition bodies, table zebra. Canonical splits raised chrome into surface-1/2/3 and the renderer only ever needed the middle one. Taking surface-2 rather than surface-1 is deliberate: the renderer has no top bar of its own (Material draws it), so what it calls raised is a panel, not chrome.

column4: Dividers, table grid lines, field borders. WARNING: canonical border is documented as serving all three at once, which is exactly why the contrast gate REMOVED its 3:1 pairs rather than failing all 19 themes on a decorative divider. Do not re-add that threshold when this lands.

column4: Primary action and link colour. base.css maps --md-typeset-a-color to it, so links are ours, not the browser's.

ok

column4: NO CANONICAL EQUIVALENT. A reference to a page that has not been written YET. The renderer's own file records why it is not danger: shared with danger it came out the same alarm red as a genuine error, on a list where most items were simply unwritten. It is a real semantic distinction -- NOT-YET-WRITTEN is not FAILED -- and canonical has no slot for it. 19 hex values are needed and they are NOT machine-derivable: D5 forbids auto-darkening by formula, which is the transform that produced the four-teams-one-red collision. Author it in the SAME pass as the per-mode re-authoring already queued, not as a half-filled column bolted onto a shape that is being retired.

column1: # CANONICAL ROLES THE RENDERER DOES NOT YET CONSUME, AND SHOULD
# These are not gaps in the renderer. They are capacity it gains for free the
# moment the refit lands, and each one already has a consumer waiting.
# accent-soft  the terminology marker class ALREADY names it (see
#              doc-render-engine/theme/marker-classes.tsv). It reports as an
#              unknown token once per build today and falls back to the body
#              colour, because the stand-in table has no second accent. This is
#              the single clearest proof the bridge is worth building: a correct
#              decision, already made, already written into one cell, that
#              cannot paint.
# data-1..4    categorical slots. The TSV data tables have column TYPES now
#              (id/num/money/text/prose, PR #55) and nothing to colour them
#              with. WARNING: D8 is live -- all four fail natively on every
#              light theme. Do not wire these up before D8 is ruled.
# text-faint   tertiary / disabled / placeholder. The renderer currently reaches
#              for ink-muted twice at two different weights.
# on-accent    text sitting on an accent fill. WARNING: D7 is live and larger
#              than it looks -- this pair misses 4.5:1 on SEVEN themes today.
# info         informational state. The renderer has no fourth semantic and
#              currently overloads accent for it.
# accent-2     secondary accent / focus ring.
# field        input fill. No consumer in a static renderer today; listed so
#              nobody records it as missing.
# COLOUR SPACE. The renderer authors in OKLCH; canonical storage is HEX and
# that is LOCKED for a real reason, not a preference -- Michael hand-copies hex
# into FileMaker's colour picker, so hex is the only format that serves the
# actual workflow. Judging in OKLCH stays correct and is unaffected. The refit
# converts one way, at build time, and stores nothing back.
# TABLE SHAPE. The renderer's table is LONG (theme, token, dark, light);
# canonical is WIDE (one row per theme, 36 columns). Do not port the wide shape
# into the renderer. Canonical is already moving toward one-row-per-mode with an
# identity grouping column, which converges on the long shape rather than away
# from it. The generator emits whatever each consumer needs; neither table is
# the other's source.
